articles.title: Service Changes on Rochdale Line Due to Planned Works Until 28 August
articles.excerpt: Planned track renewal works on the Rochdale line will affect tram services from 15 to 28 August, with bus replacements in place.
articles.content_html:
Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has announced that planned works will disrupt tram services on the Rochdale line from Saturday 15 August to Friday 28 August. During this period, a bus replacement service will operate between affected stops to ensure continued travel for passengers.

Additionally, on Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August, works will take place in Manchester city centre, specifically at Manchester Town Hall. As a result, no trams will operate via Exchange Square, with services on the East Didsbury and Trafford Centre lines rerouted via Market Street and Shudehill instead.

Passengers are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as these changes may affect travel times. Essential improvement works will also be taking place at Prestwich Metrolink stop from Monday 18 May to Wednesday 19 August, although tram services will not be directly affected at this location.

For those requiring step-free access, the lifts at Failsworth tram stop are currently out of service, and passengers are advised to travel to Hollinwood to connect to services. Customers needing assistance can contact the Metrolink customer service centre at 0161 244 1000, available from 7am to 8pm on weekdays and 8am to 8pm on weekends and bank holidays.

Big Shaq and Yahya Bamba also contributed to the team's performance, indicating a promising season ahead for Newport County. The match was marked by high energy and enthusiasm from both players and fans alike.

While the specific scoreline was not detailed, the excitement surrounding Newport's performance suggests a competitive atmosphere as the season unfolds. Fans are eager to see how the team will build on this initial success.

As the EFL season progresses, both teams will be looking to improve their standings, with Newport aiming to maintain their momentum and Rochdale seeking to bounce back in their upcoming fixtures.

articles.title: Rochdale Council Offers Support for Domestic Violence Victims
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council is providing resources and support for those affected by domestic violence and abuse, including free training for local businesses.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has launched a series of initiatives aimed at supporting victims of domestic violence and abuse. The council encourages anyone who is concerned about someone potentially being a victim to reach out for help, either through the council or Greater Manchester Police.

As part of its commitment to combat domestic abuse, the council is collaborating with White Ribbon, a charity focused on ending male violence against women and girls. This partnership includes offering free domestic abuse awareness training for businesses within the borough, aimed at equipping them to better support individuals affected by such issues.

The council's website provides comprehensive guidance on what to do if you suspect someone is being abused, including emergency contact details for various services. Resources are available for families needing support on a range of related issues, ensuring that help is accessible to those in need.

Residents are encouraged to utilise these resources and training opportunities to foster a safer community. For more information, visit the Rochdale Borough Council's dedicated page on domestic violence and abuse.

articles.title: Thousands Attend Rochdale Feel Good Festival Featuring Gabrielle
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale Feel Good Festival attracted thousands to the town centre on 8 August 2026, showcasing live music, food, and entertainment, with performances from Gabrielle and local bands.
articles.content_html:
Thousands packed Rochdale town centre on Saturday, 8 August 2026, for the Rochdale Feel Good Festival, which featured a vibrant mix of music, food, and entertainment. The event, organised by the Rochdale Development Agency, was headlined by two-time BRIT Award winner Gabrielle, alongside performances from Ash and Starsailor.

The festival commenced in the early afternoon, with large crowds gathering at the main stage located in Rochdale Town Hall Square. Councillor Georgina Jacques, assistant cabinet member for communities and co-operation at Rochdale Borough Council, expressed her delight at the turnout, noting that visitors from across the UK attended, many for the first time. She remarked on the positive feedback received, particularly praising Gabrielle's performance as a nostalgic celebration of the 90s.

The main stage was opened by local five-piece metal band Metro, who won this year's Rochdale Music Service Battle of the Bands competition. Their debut performance was well-received by the audience, showcasing the talent emerging from the local music scene. DJ Dave Sweetmore hosted the main stage, adding to the festival's lively atmosphere.

Following the festival, the Rochdale Development Agency plans to gather feedback and conduct a thorough evaluation of the event in the coming weeks. Councillor Jacques thanked all attendees, staff, partners, volunteers, and security crews for their contributions to the festival's success.

articles.title: Lift at Derker Tram Stop Out of Service Until Further Notice
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers. Alternative step-free routes are available for travel towards and away from Manchester.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop is out of service as of Friday, 14 August 2026, at 6:30pm, and will remain unavailable until further notice. This disruption affects passengers using the tram service in both directions.

For those travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is provided via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading towards Rochdale can also use a ramp from Cromford Street, followed by a track crossing to reach the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has issued an apology for any inconvenience caused by this service disruption and encourages passengers to plan their journeys accordingly.

Further updates regarding the lift's status will be provided as they become available. Passengers are advised to check the TfGM website for the latest travel alerts and information.

articles.title: Birtle Road in Heywood to Close for Roadworks from 24 August 2026
articles.excerpt: Birtle Road will be temporarily closed for roadworks from 24 August to 28 August 2026, affecting traffic flow in Heywood.
articles.content_html:
Birtle Road in Heywood will be temporarily closed for roadworks from Monday, 24 August 2026, to Friday, 28 August 2026. The closure will take place daily from 10am to 4pm, starting at the junction with Gristlehurst Lane and extending 95 metres southward.

Due to the nature of the works, there will be no alternative route for vehicles during this period. Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly to avoid delays.

The roadworks are part of ongoing improvements in the Rochdale borough aimed at enhancing local infrastructure. Further details about the roadworks can be found on the Rochdale Borough Council website.

Residents and commuters are encouraged to check for updates on the progress of the works and any potential impacts on local traffic.

articles.title: Traffic Disruptions on Manchester Road Due to Ongoing Roadworks Until April 2027
articles.excerpt: Temporary traffic lights and lane closures on Manchester Road are expected to cause delays for motorists and bus services until April 2027.
articles.content_html:
Temporary traffic lights and lane closures are currently in effect on Manchester Road in Rochdale, specifically at the junctions of Silk Street, Bolton Road, Edinburgh Way, and Rochdale Valley Way. These roadworks began on 17 May and are scheduled to continue until 10 April 2027.

Motorists should be aware that these disruptions may lead to increased congestion, particularly during peak travel times. Bus services operating through this route may also experience delays as a result of the ongoing works.

The roadworks are part of a larger initiative aimed at improving infrastructure and traffic flow in the region. However, the extended duration of these disruptions may pose challenges for local commuters and residents.

For live updates on bus services and potential delays, residents can visit the Bee Network website, which provides real-time information on departures from Rochdale Interchange.
